scenes.contextualRelevance: Thematic elements explain the intricate processes of fertilization and seed development, underpinning the life cycle of plants.

narrativeProgression.description: After pollination, the narrator explains the subsequent process of fertilization, resulting in seed production.
The scene focuses on the pollen grain landing on the stigma and developing a pollen tube that grows down to the ovary.
The male sex cells travel down the pollen tube, with one fertilizing the female egg to develop into a seed and the other forming the endosperm, which provides nourishment for the seed.
The scene shows the ovary enlarging and developing into a fruit, surrounding the seeds.
The narrator explains the dispersal of fruits and seeds, which can occur in various ways, including by humans.
The scene shows a hand planting seeds in pots, symbolizing the completion of the cycle as the seeds germinate into new plants under suitable conditions.
